title: Reconcile unattributed request activity created by proxy reconnects during regional failover
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported unexplained token/usage deltas after regional failover windows (Hosted + Dedicated + Private). Root cause appears to be a race in the proxy reconnect logic: when a connection to an upstream serving pool is dropped and re-established, a subset of in-flight requests are re-emitted without the original attribution headers (X-Tenant-ID / X-Request-Origin) and are processed by fallback pools. Those replayed requests were being recorded in the metering pipeline with partial or empty attribution, creating unattributed usage buckets and incorrect invoices.

Impact: Affected tenants saw token usage that was not tied to their ledger or appeared in the 'unattributed' bucket in billing dashboards. Some customers experienced sudden invoice increases or unexplained credits applied after manual reconciliation. This affects Hosted, Dedicated and Private clusters where proxy reconnects + routing fallback occurred during high-volume failover (not limited to a single region).

Reproduction notes: Recreated in staging by forcing 1000 concurrent streaming generation requests then bumping a simulated upstream node to DROP during active KV-cache warmup. Observed ~0.7% of requests reprocessed without X-Tenant-ID on the ingest path when the reconnect path executed. Logs show reconnect path uses a short-lived proxy socket that misses header copy in the resend code path (grpc-multiplexed flows).

Immediate mitigation (hotfix already deployed to Hosted):
- Short-term patch: ensure reconnect resend code copies complete attribution headers before re-emission. Hotpatch rolled to hosted-edge (canary -> 25% -> 100%) on 2026-03-11.
- Backfill: Add a reconciliation job to map unattributed events to likely tenant by joining on session-id and timestamp proximity (heuristic) for events in the last 7 days; this will reduce customer invoice variance while permanent fix rolls out.

Long-term fixes / design decisions:
1) Make attribution header copy atomic in proxy library; add unit tests ensuring header preservation across reconnect/resend code paths.
2) Add required header enforcement in ingest pipeline with safe-fail (reject + counter) so that replayed requests without attribution are dropped and surfaced instead of silently attributed to 'unattributed'.
3) Enhance the metering pipeline to persist original-request-id and session-id through the downstream stores so we can perform deterministic reconciliations.
4) Add an observability check: alert when unattributed bucket growth rate exceeds baseline (default 0.1% of tokens) and when reconnect rate spikes.

Rollout plan:
- Hosted: patch already deployed to runtime-1.24 (canary 2026-03-11 -> full 2026-03-12).
- Dedicated: provide patch bundle + preflight checklist to SRE and Dedicated onboarding team. Target rollout window: 2026-03-18 to avoid peak commit windows for reserved customers.
- Private/on-prem: prepare patch and install instructions; coordinate with Solutions Eng for air-gapped installs.

Monitoring & QA:
- New e2e regression test added to CI that simulates reconnects under streaming load and asserts no missing tenant attribution.
- Dashboard panels: 'unattributed token rate', 'proxy reconnect per minute', and 'replayed-request count' added to Console.

Next steps:
- Finish deterministic backfill job and run on last 30 days (priority, then fade to 7 days).
- Perform customer communications for top 12 affected accounts with reconciled numbers and credits where appropriate.
- Postmortem and follow-up EPIC to reduce single-message replay risk (ENG-130900 planned).

comments: 2026-03-10 — Maya Chen: Ticket opened after ops escalations from two enterprise customers. Initial triage indicates reconnect path may be resending without headers. Assigned to Aisha for hotfix work and ownership.

2026-03-11 — Aisha Patel: Deployed hotpatch to hosted-edge canary. Observed immediate drop in unattributed spike on canary nodes. Preparing PR with unit tests and a small refactor to the resend logic. Draft PR: edge-proxy#2876

2026-03-11 — Liam O'Connor (SRE): Ran targeted reconciliation query for yesterday's window; estimated 2.1M tokens unattributed across five customers. Suggested running heuristic backfill with session-id join. Scheduling backfill for 2026-03-13 in a controlled job.
2026-03-12 — Aisha Patel: Canary -> 25% -> 100% rollout completed. No regressions observed. Added CI e2e test that fails if any request processed without X-Tenant-ID in simulated reconnect flow.
